goal: Implement the `callisto matrix` CLI subcommand end-to-end: new MatrixReport/PlatformTarget/RuntimeVersionEntry types, a per-triple CI-scheduling table layered over the existing triple_to_role, napi/maturin/runtime-version manifest readers with hard-error and diagnostic-warning paths, the public callisto_graph::commands::matrix() entry point, CLI wiring with JSON/text rendering, and the action.yml jq pipeline that consumes it.
architecture: Bottom-up: foundational serde types land first in callisto-model (no dependents yet), then the new GraphError/DiagnosticCode variants, then a private crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs module builds up from the smallest pure function (the CI-scheduling table) through manifest readers to full-workspace assembly, each layer tested in isolation with tempdir fixtures before the next layer composes it. The public crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/matrix.rs entry point adapts a real Workspace into matrix.rs's plain-data input shape (mirroring the commands/X.rs -> X.rs split established by publish.rs/apply.rs). CLI wiring (clap args, renderer, handler) follows the exact status.rs precedent so global --format dispatch and GraphError->CliError conversion need no new mechanism. Integration tests run the real compiled binary against tempdir workspaces to prove the acceptance criteria end-to-end; action.yml wiring is the final, non-Rust step.
tech_stack: cargo test / cargo nextest (test runners; `just test` also runs `cargo nextest run --workspace || moon run :test`)
GitHub Actions composite action shell + jq (action.yml wiring)

tasks.title: Add read_napi_targets() raw package.json reader with malformed/wrong-type detection
steps: Design decision (stated explicitly, spec leaves this open): matrix.rs reads package.json directly with its own small JSON read, rather than calling crate::napi::NapiTargetsIndex::load. Reason: NapiTargetsIndex::load's `.and_then(|t| t.as_array())` silently treats a non-array `napi.targets` value as if the field were absent (returns None, no error) -- this would violate AC-010c, which requires a non-array napi.targets to be a hard parse error. NapiTargetsIndex is also keyed by GroupName (fixed-group membership), not by registered package, which is a narrower topology than a per-package matrix reader needs. This function still reuses `triple_to_role`-compatible triple strings as-is (no new recognition table) and never modifies napi.rs, satisfying the spec's actual hard constraints. package.json reads use `serde_json::Value` directly, mirroring NapiTargetsIndex's own read technique (same field paths: napi.targets).

Lint gate note: as in T04, matrix.rs's `#![allow(dead_code)]` (added in T04, removed in T12) suppresses the dead_code lint that would otherwise fire on this task's pub(crate) items before they have a non-test caller. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `just lint`/`just ci` are therefore expected to stay GREEN at this and every commit through T11 -- an attribute-level `#[allow(...)]` overrides a command-line `-D warnings` for the lint it names, in the scope it annotates. NOTE 2: crates/callisto-cli/src/main.rs:59-73 matches `cli.command` exhaustively with no wildcard arm and `Command` is not `#[non_exhaustive]`, so adding `Command::Matrix` without also touching main.rs makes the `callisto-cli` bin target fail to compile with `error[E0004]: non-exhaustive patterns`. tasks.title: Integration test: malformed and wrong-type manifests exit 1, using registration-safe fixtures (AC-010, AC-010b, AC-010c)
steps: Context: uses T22's base_workspace/run_matrix_json/assert_error_exit_no_report helpers. Every fixture below must ensure the package actually REGISTERS with the workspace locator before matrix() can reach its malformed/wrong-type manifest: crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/ignore_walk.rs silently drops a directory from package discovery entirely when its only manifest fails to parse or lacks a name field (`if let Ok(...)` with no error arm on both the package.json and pyproject.toml read sites) -- so a directory whose SOLE manifest is malformed never becomes a registered package, and matrix() (which iterates only already-registered packages) never reaches it. Each fixture below therefore pairs the malformed/wrong-type manifest under test with a co-located, valid, name-bearing manifest of the OTHER kind so the directory registers, and matrix.rs's own independent read of the malformed manifest (not the locator's silently-dropped read) is what surfaces the error.

tasks.title: Wire the real `callisto matrix` subcommand into action.yml, replacing the platformTargets stub (AC-016)
steps: Context: this task has no Rust test to write -- it is a shell/YAML change to the composite action, verified by grep assertions instead of cargo test, matching AC-016's literal byte-for-byte jq filter requirement (whitespace-insensitive) and the requirement that the '{"platformTargets":{}}' literal fallback string no longer appears. The original stub's `2>/dev/null || echo '{"platformTargets":{}}'` pattern silently swallowed a hard `callisto matrix` error (e.g. AC-010/AC-017); this task replaces that with a `set -o pipefail` guard plus an explicit `|| { echo "::error::..."; exit 1; }` so a real failure fails the step instead of producing empty output, while keeping the jq filter text byte-for-byte identical to AC-016's pinned text.

FAILING CHECK (write this first, run before editing). From the repo root:

```bash
grep -n 'platformTargets":{}}' .github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml
grep -n 'unique_by(.artifactName)' .github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml
grep -n 'set -o pipefail' .github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml
```
EXPECTED (pre-change) FAILURE: the first grep matches line 161 (the stub fallback still present); the second and third greps match nothing (exit code 1, no output) -- neither the jq filter nor the pipefail guard exist yet.

MINIMAL IMPLEMENTATION. In .github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml, replace the existing block (around line 157-162):

```yaml
          # Emit native matrix targets for downstream build jobs. The callisto
          # matrix subcommand is planned but not yet available in all releases;
          # the fallback to '{"platformTargets":{}}' ensures downstream jobs
          # that consume this output receive valid JSON and do not fail.
          NATIVE_MATRIX=$(callisto matrix --format json 2>/dev/null || echo '{"platformTargets":{}}')
          echo "nativeMatrix=$NATIVE_MATRIX" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
```

with:

```yaml
          # Emit native matrix targets for downstream build jobs, deduplicated
          # by artifactName in case the same triple is declared by more than
          # one package's platform-target group. set -o pipefail ensures a
          # hard `callisto matrix` error (e.g. malformed manifest, conflicting
          # platform-target sources) fails this step instead of silently
          # producing empty output.
          set -o pipefail
          NATIVE_MATRIX=$(callisto matrix --format json | jq -c '[.platformTargets[].targets[]] | unique_by(.artifactName)') || { echo "::error::callisto matrix failed"; exit 1; }
          echo "nativeMatrix=$NATIVE_MATRIX" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
```

(The surrounding shell wrapper's variable name and quoting style are preserved from the original; the fallback literal is removed, the real subcommand call plus the exact jq filter text `[.platformTargets[].targets[]] | unique_by(.artifactName)` are introduced per AC-016's byte-for-byte requirement on the filter text, and a `set -o pipefail` guard plus explicit error exit replace the silently-swallowing `2>/dev/null || echo ...` fallback.)

RUN (expect pass):

```bash
grep -c 'platformTargets":{}}' .github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml
grep -n 'unique_by(.artifactName)' .github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml
grep -n 'set -o pipefail' .github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml
grep -n '::error::callisto matrix failed' .github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml
```
EXPECTED OUTPUT: first command prints `0` (the stub literal is gone); second command prints the new NATIVE_MATRIX line containing the exact jq filter text; third and fourth commands each print one matching line confirming the pipefail guard and explicit error-exit are present.
tasks.commit_message: feat(action): wire callisto matrix into the nativeMatrix output with a pipefail error guard (AC-016)

reasoning:
Decomposition follows the launcher's mandated order (foundational types -> diagnostic/error variants -> CI table -> readers -> assembly -> public entry point -> CLI -> integration -> action.yml), split further wherever a single task would need more than one design decision or exceed ~15 minutes.

T01-T03 are independent leaf additions (model types, diagnostic code, graph error variant) with no dependencies on each other except T02/T03 needing T01's types to exist for round-trip test ergonomics. T02 also updates a second, independent copy of the DiagnosticCode enum embedded as documentation prose in docs/01-spec.md (distinct from the G.13 attribution table), keeping both doc locations in sync with the real enum.

T04-T11 build up crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs strictly bottom-up: the CI-scheduling table (T04) and build_platform_target (T05, now including a table-driven AC-014 test across all remaining platform families) have zero I/O and are pure-function unit tests; T06-T08 are the three raw-manifest readers; T09/T10 (originally a single 'assemble_platform_target_group' task) are split into source-selection-with-conflict-detection (T09, producing the interim `select_platform_target_source` helper) and per-triple target-building-with-diagnostics (T10, which composes T09's helper) so each half stays independently testable and under ~15 minutes; T11 is the last pure-data-in/pure-data-out function (build_matrix_report). T04 adds `#![allow(dead_code)]` to matrix.rs (removed by T12) so `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` does not block every intermediate commit through T11 -- each of T04-T11's steps says explicitly that only that task's own `cargo test` RUN command gates its completion, not `just lint`/`just ci`.

Design decision documented explicitly in T06/T07 (not left for the plan reader to infer): matrix.rs reads package.json/pyproject.toml directly with its own minimal JSON/TOML parsing rather than routing through napi::NapiTargetsIndex::load, for the two independently-verified reasons cited in those tasks' steps.

T12 is the seam where Workspace-specific code appears for the first time; it fixes `callisto_graph::config::load`'s real signature (takes the workspace root directory, not a path to callisto.toml), removes T04's dead_code allowance now that commands/matrix.rs is a real caller (restoring a clean `just lint` from this commit onward), and extends its --package-filter unit test to assert runtimeVersions is filtered symmetrically with platformTargets (AC-006 covers both maps, not just platformTargets).

T13-T15 split CLI wiring into three single-purpose tasks (clap surface, renderer, handler) specifically because the handler's Text arm needs render_matrix to already exist to compile.

T16-T19 are black-box integration tests run against the fully-implemented CLI binary via CARGO_BIN_EXE_callisto. T18 (--package filter) additionally asserts runtimeVersions filtering, mirroring T12's unit-level fix. T20 and T21 are new tasks closing two previously-under-covered contracts: T20 covers AC-011's full diagnostic contract (a render_matrix unit test with a non-empty diagnostics vec, plus a binary-spawning integration test proving exit 0, exactly one diagnostic, the bad triple's exclusion from every targets[] array, and every other recognised triple's survival); T21 covers AC-008/AC-003b's CLI-level gap (bare invocation and explicit --format text must both exit 0 and produce byte-identical non-JSON output), which previously had only unit-level (render_matrix, clap-parsing) coverage.

T22/T23 split what was one oversized task (three shared helpers plus four error-path tests spanning AC-010/AC-010b/AC-010c/AC-017) into: T22 (shared helpers -- base_workspace, run_matrix_json, assert_error_exit_no_report -- plus the one test needing no registration workaround, AC-017's conflicting-sources case, since both its manifests are independently well-formed and name-bearing); and T23 (the malformed/wrong-type tests, corrected to satisfy the locator's silent-drop behavior: crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/ignore_walk.rs drops any directory whose sole manifest fails to parse or lacks a name field, so AC-010's malformed pyproject.toml now sits alongside a valid, name-bearing package.json in the same directory -- and symmetrically for AC-010b's malformed package.json alongside a valid pyproject.toml -- and AC-010c's wrong-type fixtures now all carry a valid "name"/[project].name field so ignore_walk.rs actually registers them, plus two new sibling AC-010c cases for [tool.maturin].targets-as-a-string and engines.node-as-a-number that the original plan's AC-010c coverage was missing entirely).

T24 (action.yml) is last because it has no Rust test and no compile dependency on anything except the binary existing and behaving per AC-016's exact CLI invocation -- it is verified with grep instead of cargo test, and now also replaces the original silently-swallowing `2>/dev/null || echo fallback` with a `set -o pipefail` guard and explicit error exit so a hard `callisto matrix` failure (AC-010/AC-017) fails the composite-action step instead of producing empty nativeMatrix output, while keeping the jq filter text byte-for-byte identical to AC-016's pinned requirement.

Everything the spec pinned verbatim (MatrixReport/PlatformTargetGroup/PlatformTarget/RuntimeVersionEntry field lists with no rid/targetFrameworks, the 18-triple hostRunner/useCross/artifactName table, GraphError::ConflictingPlatformTargetSources's E118 code/field list/error+help text, DiagnosticCode::UnrecognisedPlatformTriple's kebab-case value in both docs/01-spec.md locations, the write_json-not-write_report_json choice, and PackageId::name() as the map-key accessor) is reproduced byte-for-byte from the spec's api_surface and acceptance_criteria in the relevant task's implementation code, not re-derived.

Deliberately deferred, not an oversight: `callisto schema` (crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/schema.rs) does not gain a `matrix` arm, and docs/01-spec.md's/README.md's/ARCHITECTURE.md's CLI command tables are not updated to list `matrix`. SPEC-004 has no acceptance criterion for either -- its only documentation requirement is the G.13 diagnostic-attribution row (T02), which this plan implements. Recording this explicitly so a future canon-verifier drift pass does not misread the absence as an implementation gap; it is out of this spec's scope by design and would need its own AC in a follow-up spec if wanted.
